findings.source: Accounting.sol:524 Math.saturatingSub(currentShares, requiredShares) (OZ trySub: c = a - b; success = c <= a; result = c * toUint(success))
findings.issue: The saturating subtraction c * (c <= a) is printed with the product distributed over c = a - b, so the comparison is repeated and the expression (used up to four times per function) reads as an arithmetic puzzle instead of 'a - b if b <= a else 0'.
findings.rule: Do not distribute a product over a sum when that duplicates a factor; with wrapping arithmetic 'a - b <= a' is 'b <= a'; x * bool(c) prints as 'x if c else 0' (or a saturating-sub helper).

findings.issue: The zero-initialisation of a new struct array is a rotated count-down loop with its first element peeled (P3); event data written at mem[mem[64]] is printed as raw memory because of the free-memory-pointer self-alias (4 logs, 9 'return memory').

notes: All 94 ABI functions and the fallback reviewed; no semantic error found. Small getters and setters read directly; the deposit / claim / penalize / settle / compensate functions (170-490 lines) by structure (call order, BondCore share accounting with SafeMath subs, BondLock checks, events). The BondCurvesLib functions are external (delegatecall to the library: addBondCurve, updateBondCurve, getBondAmountByKeysCount, getKeysCountByBondAmount...), so BondCurvesLib._check / _addIntervals and the binary-search loops run in the library, not in this bytecode; the pack's reach list also names MetaRegistry._storeExternalOperators, which this contract does not contain. Source loops in this bytecode: _validateFeeSplits, _updateFeeSplits (with the 'delete' clearing loop, implicit), getFeeSplitTransfers (also inlined in _pullAndSplitFeeRewards) and _pullAndSplitFeeRewards' transfer loop: all readable whiles. Implicit: ABI copies of the calldata BondCurveIntervalInput[] for the delegatecall and the event (P7), storage-to-memory struct-array copies, the zeroed struct-array allocation (P3, 5 copies). getCurveInfo's two checks (InvalidBondCurveId on curveId > length - 1 unchecked, then Panic(50)) are both needed (length 0). P11: bounds checks of transfers[i] under i < transfers.length.
summary: Faithful on every path checked; the main readability problems are OZ's saturatingSub printed as a distributed boolean product (26 lines), 2-slot struct arrays shown as flat word arrays, and the usual memory issues (keccak scratch stores, event data and returns as raw memory).
